text:
jordan: Hey team — opened my very first PR to add server-side rate limiting for the user profile endpoints (branch feat/profile-rate-limit). I'm a little fuzzy on our review flow and whether we should squash or preserve commits. Also, any tips for the PR description?

miriam: Welcome, jordan! :wave: Short guidance: keep commits while iterating, then tidy up before merge. Our repo uses the merge queue, so we generally want a single clean merge commit on main. You can either squash locally or rely on the repo's auto-squash-on-merge setting — but please mark the PR title and body clearly.

jordan: Cool, where do I indicate the desired merge behavior?

toni: Put a one-line summary at the top of the PR and a short bulleted checklist. Example header: "PROF-210: server-side rate limit for profile writes". Then fill out the template sections: What, Why, How to test, Rollout plan. Add the label `ready-for-merge` when you want the merge queue to pick it up.

jordan: Thanks — our pre-commit hooks flagged a bunch of imports and a minor type error. I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` but CI still failed one integration test. Any quick debugging tips?

miriam: For flaky integration tests, run `pytest tests/integration -k <test_name> -q` locally with `--maxfail=1` and look at the test log. If it times out in CI but passes locally, add a comment with the failing job URL and the label `ci-flaky`. We also have a local test harness: `make test-integration-local` which spins up a lightweight deps stack.

toni: Also check for test-order sensitivity — some integration tests depend on the stateful store. Use `pytest -k <test> -x` and `--random-order-bucket=module` if you suspect ordering issues. If you fix a flake, include a short note in the PR describing the cause.

jordan: Good to know. About commit messages — do we have a required format? I used conventional commits but not sure if that's expected.

miriam: We don't strictly enforce Conventional Commits, but we like `area(scope): short summary`. Example: `profile(write): add token-bucket limiter for user updates`. Keep the body to explain non-obvious tradeoffs. If you rely on a feature flag, mention the flag name and rollout plan.

toni: If your change introduces a new config knob, add a default in `config/defaults.yml` and include migration notes. For anything that touches DB schema or public API, add `needs-product` label and ping the product owner.

jordan: Okay. Also saw a bot comment about "auto-merge: safelist" in another PR — do we have an auto-merge whitelist?

miriam: Yes — the merge queue will auto-merge if all required checks pass and the PR has the `ready-for-merge` label and no blocking reviews. Certain sensitive areas (deploy, infra, public-api) are gatekept by CODEOWNERS and won't auto-merge without explicit approval.

pr-helper-bot: tip: to re-request reviewers after pushing new commits, comment `@pr-helper-bot re-request` and the bot will ping the CODEOWNERS.

jordan: Great. One last question: if I need a very small follow-up change (typo fix), is it okay to push it as separate commit after approval, or should it be squashed into the original?

toni: For tiny fixes post-review, prefer a small separate commit and call it out in the comment. If it changes semantics, re-request review. When the PR lands via merge queue, maintainers may squash for history hygiene.

miriam: Also add a short "How I tested this" section with reproducible steps in the PR body. Example: `make dev && curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/profiles/123 -H \"Authorization: Bearer ...\" -d '{\"bio\":\"x\"}'` and show observed rate-limit headers.

jordan: Perfect — thanks everyone, I'll update the PR with the checklist, run the integration harness, and mark ready when green. Appreciate the quick onboarding help! :pray:
